nfigurations that define how MCPJam\n connects to and talks to your MCP servers. The original `/hosts` paths\n remain as
deprecated, ID-only compatibility aliases with their original\n DTOs and their original (tokenless) write contracts; every a

lias response
 carries `Deprecation: true`. New integrations should use `/clients`.
 - name: Environments
 description
: >-\n Project environments: named, live-editable execution bundles (one host, an\n optional standalone server group, op
tionally pinned skills and plugin\n versions) that eval suites and goals run against. Distinct from Sandbox\n images, wh

description: >-
 Agent Plugins imported into a project — read-only inventory and version
 detail.
 - name: Skills
description: >-\n Cloud Skills: authored SKILL.md files stored in a project. Read-only here.\n Environments pin skil
ls by id (`skillSelection.skillIds`) and eval runs\n pin them with `--compose-skill`, so this surface exists to give an\n

unattended caller those ids; authoring is an app flow behind a beta gate.
 - name: Sandbox images
 description: >-
Custom Computer images: a digest-pinned Dockerfile built into an immutable\n image your project's computers boot from.\n - n

ame: Server diagnostics
 description: Connect-level health checks against a saved MCP server.
 - name: Primitives
 descr
iption: 'The server''s MCP primitives: tools, prompts, and resources.'\n - name: Export\n description: Full-server snapshots f

or diffing and CI.
 - name: Execution
 description: 'Run the server''s primitives: call tools, render prompts.'
 - name: E

val runs
 description: >-
 Asynchronous eval suite runs: create with 202, poll status, iterations,
 and traces.

- name: Conformance runs
 description: >-
 Ingest MCP spec-conformance results from the SDK/CLI into project-owned

history. Distinct from Eval runs (authored LLM cases) and from directory
 readiness.
 - name: Server connections
 d

escription: >-
 Connect an MCP server URL to a project, authorizing in a browser when the
 server requires it.
 - na

me: Server accounts
 description: >-
 The accounts a saved server signs in with, addressed by id or by name.
 Toke
ns are write-only: an upload takes them and no route returns one.\n - name: OAuth\n description: 'Bring-your-own OAuth: import

externally obtained tokens for a server.'
 - name: Studies
 description: >-
 Publish a project environment as a **stu
dy** for people outside the\n project to talk to, read what they did, and control who can reach it.\n Several of these N
projectId}/scenarios/{scenarioId}`,\n `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` and\n `/projects/{pr
ojectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` — keep\n working and are deliberately not documented here. They return their\
n original bodies, which spell the owning id `scenarioId` and whose detail\n read carries no execution settings, and eve
ry response answers with\n `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming its successor. They are\n removed at general a

vailability; a new integration should use the paths on
 this page.
 - name: Catalog
 description: >-
 Discover t
he resources the other routes operate on: your account,\n projects, servers, eval suites, and chat sessions.\n - name: Tunne

ls
 description: >-
 Relay tunnels that expose local MCP servers through a public URL,
 registered as first-class

project servers (the `mcpjam cloud tunnel` CLI
 flow).
 - name: Agent
 description: >-
 Headless agent turns ove
r the public API: send a message history, the\n server runs one assistant turn with project-scoped workspace tools (eval\n
reads + suite creation) on a pinned hosted model, and returns the reply\n plus created-resource references.\n - name: Swa

rms
 description: >-
 Personas, journeys and swarm containers — the authoring half of Swarms —
 plus the model-bac

ked generation that drafts them.
 - name: Swarm runs
 description: >-
 Launching journeys and reading what they produc

ed. Launching SPENDS — see
 the per-operation notes.
 - name: Swarm insights
 description: >-
 What a swarm run
revealed. The scorecard and findings are deterministic\n and free; requesting wave insights runs models and draws on your sha

red
 daily ledger.
 - name: Directory readiness
 description: >-
 Grade a saved server against a publisher's lis
ting requirements:\n Anthropic's connector directory or OpenAI's plugin directory. Reported as\n lane status and coverag
e, never as a numeric score, and excluded from\n `pooledConformanceScore`. Deterministic grading is free; model-backed\n
experience observations are an explicit opt-in whose model cost is on\n MCPJam — no credits are consumed — and they can neve

r decide a verdict.
 - name: Registry
 description: >-
 Search the scraped MCP directories (Claude, ChatGPT, and any f
uture\n source), list curated/org registry cards, and install them into a project.\n Install writes a `servers` row and
provenance — it does not open a live\n session. There is no catalog-uninstall route: delete the project server\n instead
. Directory reads require a bearer (including minted guest tokens)\n but do not materialize a user. Card/connection reads and

all writes are
 authed-non-guest.
 - name: Feedback
 description: >-
 Feedback about MCPJam itself (bugs, missi
ng capabilities, confusing\n behavior), sent to the MCPJam team and kept for 180 days. The\n `send_feedback` MCP tool ca

lls the same endpoint.

 - Catalog
 summary: Read the organization's spend budget
 descr
iption: >-\n The ceiling on what this organization may spend on MCPJam-billed work —\n chat, evals, judges and compu

ter time — in the current billing window,
 and how much of it has been spent.


 Any member may read it: a membe
r who cannot raise the ceiling still\n needs to know it exists, because it is what refused their run. `capUsd:\n nul

l` means the organization is uncapped, which is the default.


 Runs that use your own provider keys are never counted a

gainst the
 budget and never blocked by it. Neither is the free daily allowance — it
 is not credits.
